n549a5bd980f.s: Which European power arrived in India next after the Portuguese?
n549a5bd980f.x: After the Portuguese (1498) came the Dutch, with their factory at Masulipatnam in 1605; the English got the Surat farman only in 1613.

ncb3b2c4e89a.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Dutch East India Company?
o: The States-General granted it sovereign powers
It could wage war, build forts and conclude treaties
It was given only the right to collect customs duties in Indian ports
ncb3b2c4e89a.x: The States-General gave the VOC (1602) sovereign powers such as making war, building forts and concluding treaties, not merely a right to collect customs.

n27820adfb75.s: The convoy system that backed the Portuguese Cartaz system was known as:
n27820adfb75.x: The Cartaz system was backed by the Caes convoy system and customs duties.

na3614867999.s:
Consider the following statements about Portuguese defeats by the English:
1. The Battle of Swally was fought in 1612.
2. The Portuguese lost Ormuz in 1622 to the English and the Shah of Persia.
3. The defeat off Jask came before the Battle of Swally.
na3614867999.x: Swally was in 1612 and Ormuz was lost in 1622; the defeat off Jask (1620) came after Swally, so statement 3 is wrong.

new.s: In which year did the Ottoman Sultan Mehmed II capture Constantinople?
new.x: Mehmed II took Constantinople in 1453, closing the main overland route to India; 1452 is a common wrong date.

new.s: Before the sea route was found, the Asian goods brought by Arab traders were distributed in Europe mainly by:
new.x: The trade was controlled by Arabs, and Venice and Genoa distributed the goods in Europe.

new.s: Who set up naval training centres in Portugal and was the first European to actively promote navigation?
new.x: Prince Henry 'the Navigator' of Portugal set up naval training centres.

new.s: During the Age of Discovery, the caravel was a:
new.x: The caravel was a ship and the astrolabe an instrument; together they made long voyages safer.

new.s: John Cabot, who reached North America in 1497, sailed for:
new.x: John Cabot sailed for England, not Portugal.

new.s: Who made the first circumnavigation of the globe?
new.x: Ferdinand Magellan, sailing for Spain, made the first circumnavigation of the globe.

new.s: Christopher Columbus, who reached the Americas in 1492, was sponsored by:
new.x: Columbus sailed for Spain; Portugal sponsored the eastern route of Dias, da Gama and Cabral.

new.s: The 'Cape of Storms' reached by Dias in 1488 was renamed the Cape of Good Hope by:
new.x: King John II of Portugal renamed it the Cape of Good Hope.

new.s: The Treaty of Tordesillas (1494) drew the dividing meridian at how many leagues west of Cape Verde?
new.x: The Tordesillas line lay 370 leagues west of Cape Verde.

new.s: The papal bull Inter caetera (1493), dividing new lands between Spain and Portugal, was issued by Pope:
new.x: Inter caetera was issued in 1493 by Pope Alexander VI.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Treaty of Tordesillas:
1. It was signed in 1494.
2. Lands east of its line went to Spain.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The treaty was signed in 1494; lands east of the line went to Portugal and west to Spain.

new.s: In 1498 Vasco da Gama landed at ____, near Calicut.
new.x: Da Gama reached Calicut on 20 May 1498, landing at Kappad near Calicut.

new.s: After Vasco da Gama's first voyage, the spices he brought were sold in Portugal at about how many times their cost?
new.x: Back in Portugal in 1499, the spices sold at 60 times the cost.

new.s: With how many ships did Vasco da Gama leave Lisbon on 8 July 1497?
new.x: He left with four ships: Sao Gabriel, Sao Rafael, Berrio and a supply ship.

new.s: Who ruled Delhi when Vasco da Gama reached Calicut in 1498?
new.x: The Delhi ruler in 1498 was Sikandar Lodi, not Ibrahim Lodi.

new.s: The Danish East India Company was formed in:
new.x: The Danish company was formed in 1616; English 1600, Dutch 1602, French 1664.

new.s: Which company, founded in 1602, is widely called the first joint-stock company to sell shares to the public?
new.x: The Dutch VOC (1602) is widely called the first joint-stock company to sell shares to the public.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the European companies?
o: The English East India Company was chartered in 1600
The Dutch set up their first factory at Masulipatnam in 1605
The Danes had their base at Tranquebar
The French company was formed in 1616
new.x: The French company was formed in 1664; 1616 is the year of the Danish company.

new.s: Which was the Europeans' first port in Andhra?
new.x: Machilipatnam was the Europeans' first Andhra port; the Dutch set up their first factory in India there in 1605.

new.s: In July 2025 India-Brazil ties, dating to Cabral's arrival in Brazil in 1500, were recalled during the PM's visit for the:
new.x: The PM's July 2025 visit was for the 17th BRICS Summit.

new.s: The English Charter of 31 December 1600 gave the East India Company a monopoly of East Indies trade for:
new.x: Elizabeth I's charter gave a 15-year monopoly, later made perpetual.

new.s: According to the APPSC key, the English Charter of 1600 gave the Company:
new.x: The 1600 Charter gave exclusive trading rights, not territorial or legislative powers.

new.s: The first Danish factory in India was set up in 1620 at:
new.x: The Danes set up their first factory at Tranquebar (1620); Serampore came in 1755.

new.s: At Calicut in 1498, Vasco da Gama was received by the:
new.x: Vasco da Gama was received by the Zamorin of Calicut.

new.s: Vasco da Gama reached India by sailing:
o: Round the Cape of Good Hope
new.x: His route went round the Cape of Good Hope to Calicut.

new.s: The Portuguese forts at Cannanore and Anjediva (1505) were built by:
new.x: Almeida built the forts at Cannanore and Anjediva in 1505.

new.s: Who moved the Portuguese headquarters from Cochin to Goa in 1530?
new.x: Nuno da Cunha (1529-38) moved the headquarters from Cochin to Goa in 1530.

new.s: Which ruler allowed Albuquerque to build a fort at Bhatkal for the horse trade?
new.x: Krishnadeva Raya allowed the Bhatkal fort, linked to the horse trade.

new.s: The English traveller Ralph Fitch visited the court of:
new.x: Ralph Fitch came in the 1580s, in Akbar's reign.

new.s: Captain William Hawkins came to Jahangir's court as the envoy of:
new.x: Hawkins (came 1608) was the envoy of James I.

new.s: Which title did Jahangir give to William Hawkins?
new.x: Hawkins received the title 'English Khan', though his Surat permission was withdrawn under Portuguese pressure.

new.s: Edward Terry, at Jahangir's court, was the chaplain of:
new.x: Edward Terry was Sir Thomas Roe's chaplain.

new.s: In which year did Job Charnock settle at Sutanuti?
new.x: Job Charnock reached Sutanuti in 1690; Fort William followed in 1700.

new.s: Pondicherry, the French headquarters, was founded in 1674 by:
new.x: Francois Martin founded Pondicherry (1674); Caron set up the Surat factory.

new.s: The French bought Karaikal in 1739 from the:
new.x: Karaikal was bought from the Raja of Tanjore in 1739.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about French settlements:
1. Masulipatnam (1669) was a grant from the Sultan of Golconda.
2. Mahe lies on the Coromandel coast.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The 1669 Masulipatnam grant came from the Sultan of Golconda; Mahe (1725) is on the Malabar coast.

new.s: Which French enclave lies in the Godavari delta of Andhra?
new.x: Yanam (1723) in the Godavari delta is one of the four French enclaves.

new.s: The French settlement at Yanam was established in:
new.x: Yanam dates from 1723 and was re-occupied in 1731.

new.s: In the Battle of Colachel (1741), Marthanda Varma of Travancore defeated the:
new.x: At Colachel in 1741 Travancore under Marthanda Varma beat the Dutch.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
new.x: At Bedara (1759) the English under Forde beat the Dutch; Wandiwash was against the French, Colachel was won by Travancore and Swally by the English.

new.s: Which of the following was NOT brought to India by the Portuguese?
new.x: The Portuguese brought tobacco, cashew and maize, but not tea, coffee or rubber.

new.s: The Danes sold Serampore and Tranquebar to the British in:
new.x: The Danes sold both bases to the British in 1845.

new.s: The Portuguese state in Asia was known as the:
new.x: Their Asian state was the Estado da India, with HQ first at Cochin and later Goa.

new.s: Goa (1510) was the first European territory in India since:
new.x: Goa was the first European territory in India since Alexander.

new.s: The Blue Water Policy of the Portuguese was introduced by:
new.x: Almeida introduced the Blue Water Policy of naval mastery of the Indian Ocean; Albuquerque reversed it.

new.s: Who shifted the Portuguese headquarters from Cochin to Goa in 1530?
new.x: Nino (Nuno) da Cunha moved the headquarters to Goa in 1530.

new.s: The Portuguese 'marriage policy' of mixed marriages was promoted by:
new.x: Albuquerque, the real founder of Portuguese power, promoted mixed marriages.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Afonso de Albuquerque:
1. He took Goa from Bijapur in 1510.
2. He continued Almeida's Blue Water Policy.
3. He abolished Sati in his territories.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Albuquerque took Goa (1510) and abolished Sati in his territories, but he reversed the Blue Water Policy in favour of territorial conquest.

new.s: The Gujarat ruler who allowed Nuno da Cunha to build the Diu fort in 1535 was:
new.x: Bahadur Shah of Gujarat, pressed by Humayun, let da Cunha build the Diu fort; it was not Mahmud Begada.

new.s: The Portuguese gained full control of Diu by conquest in:
new.x: Diu: 1509 battle, 1535 fort, 1546 conquest.

new.s: The Portuguese obtained Bassein in 1534 from:
new.x: Bassein came from Bahadur Shah of Gujarat in 1534.

new.s: The Portuguese church at San Thome (Mylapore), 1523, was built over the tomb of:
new.x: San Thome church was built over the tomb of St. Thomas.

new.s: The Portuguese church at Bandel, near Hugli, was built in:
new.x: Bandel church dates from 1599; Hugli was granted in 1579 and lost in 1632.

new.s: Shaista Khan, Bengal governor under Aurangzeb, captured which places while suppressing the Arakanese pirates?
new.x: Shaista Khan captured Sondip and Chittagong and suppressed the Arakanese pirates.

new.s: Shah Jahan's Bengal governor who defeated the Portuguese at Hugli in 1632 was:
new.x: In 1632 Qasim Khan, Shah Jahan's Bengal governor, defeated the Portuguese at Hugli.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a New World crop brought by the Portuguese?
new.x: Tomato, chilli and tobacco came with the Portuguese from the New World; wheat did not.

new.s: The Portuguese press at Goa printed the Bible in which languages?
new.x: The Goa press (1556) printed the Bible in Kannada and Malayalam.

new.s: Under the Cartaz system, a ship found sailing without a pass was:
o: Let go after paying a fine
new.x: A ship without a Cartaz was confiscated or sunk.

new.s: In which year was Portugal merged with Spain, weakening Portuguese power in India?
new.x: Portugal merged with Spain in 1580, a cause of Portuguese decline.

new.s: Nagapattinam was lost by the Portuguese to the Dutch in:
new.x: Nagapattinam went to the Dutch in 1658; Pulicat in 1610 and Cochin in 1663.

new.s: Operation Vijay freed Goa from Portuguese rule on:
new.x: Operation Vijay freed Goa on 19 December 1961; statehood came in May 1987.

new.s: The Machilipatnam factory of 1669-70, allowed by Abdullah Qutb Shah, belonged to the:
new.x: That factory was French, the last Europeans in Andhra, not Portuguese.
